positions.as_written: Read a rotatory test as the more informative one when anterior cruciate function is in question, since it loads the coupled pair.
Expect a knee with a meniscal and a ligament injury to behave worse than either alone, because both act on the same path.
Treat coupling as the reason rotatory laxity and translational laxity dissociate after reconstruction.
Assess rotation as well as translation before calling a reconstruction successful.
Consider the coupled contribution of slope and lateral plateau shape when a graft fails without a new injury.
Repair or preserve the lateral meniscus posterior horn where possible, on mechanical grounds related to the coupled motion.
